title: SDK local prefetch, mirroring, and cache-encoder playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:
This playbook documents opinionated SDK patterns, quickstart templates, and API examples for three developer-facing primitives used across Redwood product integrations: local prefetch agents, request mirroring proxies, and cache encoders (on-client compressed caches). The guidance is focused on developer sandboxes, integration tests, and production-safe patterns for client-side or edge microservice caching that reduce token spend and improve iteration velocity without sacrificing fidelity or reproducibility.

When to use these patterns:
- Prefetch agent: warm predictable tokens or context before interactive flows (e.g., user opens chat thread).
- Mirroring proxy: duplicate a subset of production traffic to a staging runtime for A/B validation without impacting primary path.
- Cache encoder: store compressed KV or prefix caches locally to rehydrate model state faster across short sessions.

Goals and constraints:
- Preserve deterministic request/response mapping for offline replay and debugging.
- Ensure telemetry and request IDs are preserved through the pipeline.
- Provide safe defaults that avoid serving stale, high-entropy completions to users.

Design primitives and examples:
1) Local prefetch agent (pattern):
- Role: proactive fetcher that requests model outputs for templated prompts and stores them in a local cache for low-latency reuse.
- Minimal contract: async background worker, backoff on failure, eviction based on TTL and LRU, consistent telemetry.
- Example behavior: when user enters a product screen, queue generation for top-3 prompt templates relevant to that screen.

Code snippet (pseudo-YAML config for a prefetch agent):
```
name: prefetch-agent:browser-boot
trigger: on_screen_open
templates:
  - id: welcome_snippet_v2
    prompt: "You are Redwood guide: summarize features for {product_name}."
    max_tokens: 120
cache_ttl_seconds: 900
max_parallel_prefetch: 4
prefetch_backoff: {initial_ms: 200, multiplier: 2, max_ms: 5000}
eviction_policy: lru
```

2) Mirroring proxy (pattern):
- Role: transparent HTTP proxy that duplicates a controlled percentage of live requests to a staging endpoint while returning only the primary response. Useful for quality regression detection and telemetry parity checks.
- Safety: strip customer-identifying metadata before sending to staging (mask PII), obey privacy flags, respect feature flags.
- Sampling approach: deterministic hashing of request ID to ensure stable sampling across retries.

CLI example to run a local mirror proxy in dev mode:
- Start proxy: ./mirror-proxy --listen :8080 --target https://staging-inference.redwood.internal --sample-rate 0.05 --mask-headers Authorization,Cookie
- Health check: curl http://localhost:8080/health

3) Cache encoder (pattern):
- Role: compact serialization of model prefix/KV-cache or deterministic completion fragments into a compressible on-disk format for quick rehydrate.
- Requirements: versioned encoder headers, model-id compatibility check, clear byte-size limits.

Encoder metadata header example (JSON):
```
{
  "encoder_version": "v1",
  "model": "redwood-open-7b-v1",
  "created_at": "2026-02-12T10:22:00Z",
  "ttl_seconds": 3600
}
```

Operational configs (table):
- cache_ttl_seconds: 3600 (default) - how long local cached entries remain valid
- max_cache_size_mb: 50 - per-client disk budget for encoded caches
- batch_window_ms: 20 - grouping interval for bundler before sending to runtime
- max_prefetch_parallel: 4 - cap parallel prefetch jobs per client
- sample_rate_mirror: 0.01 - default mirror sampling for production
- eviction_policy: lru | time_based - default lru

SLOs and developer expectations for sandbox use:
- Prefetch latency (on-cache-hit): < 25ms additional overhead to request path.
- Cache hit rate goal for templated workflows: >= 40% for first 60s of activity.
- Mirror telemetry lag: < 5s end-to-end into staging traces.
- Safety: mirror sampling must never exceed bucketed privacy budget and must be manually enabled for new customers.

Templates included (quickstart artifacts):
1) response-bundler-template (JavaScript): an express middleware that aggregates multiple client prompts into a bundled multi-request for lower token cost and controlled latency.
2) mirror-proxy-template (Go): lightweight HTTP reverse proxy with deterministic sampling, header-masking, and spike-protection circuit breaker.
3) encoder-cli-template (Python): build/inspect/rehydrate encoded cache blobs with validation hooks and size reporting.

Deployment and rollout checklist (developer-to-production):
1. Local dev: enable prefetch agent with cache_ttl_seconds reduced to 60 to avoid stale data.
2. Integration test: run mirror-proxy with --sample-rate 1.0 against a staging model, ingest traces into observability sandbox.
3. Canary: enable mirror sampling 1% in production for 24 hours, monitor quality regressions and error spikes.
4. Gradual roll: increment sample rate and on-device prefetch within 1–2 week windows, maintain runbook-held abort criteria.

Abort criteria and runbook triggers:
- If staging mirrored requests show a completion divergence rate > 4% for gold prompt-set, rollback mirror and open triage.
- If cache-encoded rehydrate failure rate > 1% for attempts, disable decoder usage and serve cold path.
- If bundle latency (p95) > 300ms, reduce batch_window_ms by 50% and throttle prefetch concurrency.

Monitoring and tracing guidance:
- Metrics to emit: prefetch_count, prefetch_failures, cache_hit, cache_miss, mirror_sent, mirror_failures, encoder_size_bytes, bundle_latency_ms_p50/p95.
- Trace tags: request_id, mirror_sampled=true/false, encoder_version.
- Dashboards: one dev sandbox dashboard (prefetch & cache), one staging parity dashboard (mirror comparisons), one production safety dashboard (sampling and privacy budget).

Canonical fixes for top support issues (triage checklist):
1) Symptom: Prefetching causes noisy background failures and token spikes.
   Fix: verify backoff and circuit breaker config, reduce max_prefetch_parallel, and confirm telemetry filtering removed sensitive tokens before logging.
2) Symptom: Mirror proxy increases tail latency on main path.
   Fix: ensure mirror is fully asynchronous, use non-blocking fire-and-forget with bounded queue and circuit breaker; re-run load test.
3) Symptom: Encoded cache rehydrate mismatch (model version mismatch).
   Fix: add encoder_version and model-id checks in rehydrate flow and reject incompatible blobs with clear error code; auto-invalidate caches older than 24 hours by default.

Support escalations: when to open a support ticket:
- Any privacy/masking failure observed while mirroring traffic.
- Rehydrate failures impacting > 0.5% of active sessions for > 15 minutes.
- Unexpected token-cost regressions attributable to prefetch.

Ownership and contributors:

- Secondary owners: Observability team (Diego Alvarez), Security review (Priya Kapoor).
- Suggest PR reviewers: SDK authors and one infra engineer.

Appendix: quickstart commands and examples
- Initialize local dev sandbox (Dockerized bundler + mirror): ./scripts/dev-sandbox up --with-mirror --with-encoder
- Run encoder validator: python tools/encoder_cli.py validate ./tmp/cache_blob.bin
- Example API call bundling payload (JSON):
```
POST /v1/sdk/bundle
Headers: {"Authorization": "Bearer <dev-token>", "x-client-id":"dev-local-1"}
Body:
{
  "requests": [
    {"prompt": "Summarize features for product X", "max_tokens": 64},
    {"prompt": "Short tagline for product X", "max_tokens": 24}
  ],
  "bundle_hint": "low_latency"
}
```

Notes and future work:
- Investigate model-aware cache encoders that include compacted KV caches keyed by tokenizer segments.
- Provide a community-contributed set of safe prompt templates for prefetching across popular integrations.
- Automate mirror privacy validation with an offline PII detector as part of the CI pipeline.
